title: Colour
ask: What colour should the car be when it is done?
why: The colour decides how deep the paint job has to go: the same colour can stop at the outside panels, while any change means painting the door jambs, under the hood and the hatch opening as well. It also sets which paint is bought and roughly what it costs. A wrap is off the table: you ruled real paint (D-425).
options:
(a) Keep Sunbeam Silver, the factory colour (Mazda K3, confirm on the colour plate). Easiest to match, the car reads as original, and a colour match means the door jambs, under the hood and the hatch opening can stay as they are.
(b) Another factory Mazda colour of the era, e.g. Brilliant Black (PZ), Sunrise Red (RH) or Aurora White (WN). Period-correct but a change: the jambs, under the hood and the hatch opening must be painted too, or the old silver shows every time a door opens - more work and more money.
(c) A modern or custom colour, your pick. Same extra work as (b), and the paint price ranges widely by colour.
recommend: (a), unless you already have a colour in mind - then (b) or (c) and name it in words.
stops: The paint's parts list and cost (work C03), and how deep the job goes (block 04.04).

title: Who does the work
ask: Who should do the body work and the painting - a shop, you, or a split between the two?
why: This is the biggest money choice in the project. It decides whether the project buys tools and materials or buys quotes, and how many of your weekends go into it. Your bar (D-425) is body work that looks factory-designed - moulded bumpers, a reshaped rear panel, maybe flares - and that is custom fabrication and filler work where skill shows most, which weighs toward a shop for at least the shaping and the paint.
options:
(a) A body shop does all of it: rust repair, dents, prep and paint. The most expensive (a full quality respray on a car this age is often several thousand dollars, confirm with quotes), the least of your time, and the best finish.
(b) You do the rust repair, dents and sanding at home; a shop does only the spraying. Saves a good part of the cost, since prep is most of a shop's hours, but it takes many weekends, and some shops will not spray over someone else's prep.
(c) You do all of it, including spraying. Cheapest in money, but needs a spray gun, a compressor big enough for it, a clean space to spray in, and practice; the finish is the hardest part to get right.
(d) Decide after the rust survey: until you know how much rust there is, the job's size is unknown.
recommend: (b), unless the survey (B02) finds rust in the sills, floors or rear arches - structural repair and the spraying belong to a shop, so then (a). Answer now with the route you would take if the rust is light; the survey can change it.
stops: The cost estimate and parts list (work C03), and getting quotes.

title: How deep the paint goes
why: Each step adds trim to remove, masking, paint and hours - and painting the engine bay ties this project to the engine swap. Your bar (D-425) that the car looks designed that way means every filled trim hole and new panel is painted to match with no visible blend line.
options:
(a) The outside only: every panel you see with the doors, hood and hatch shut. Enough if the colour stays the same (block 04.01 (a)).
(b) The outside plus the door jambs, the underside of the hood and the hatch opening. Needed for a colour change; more masking, more trim off, more paint.
(c) Everything in (b) plus the engine bay, done while the engine is out for the LS swap (02-engine). The only time the bay is bare; it waits for the swap, and the car cannot move without an engine meanwhile.
(d) Only the panels that need repair, blended into the old paint. Cheapest, but the old paint is about 40 years old and an exact blend is unlikely.
recommend: (a) if the colour stays silver, (b) if it changes; (c) only if you want a show-quality bay and are happy to wait for the swap.
stops: The list of trim and seals to remove (work C02) and the paint quantity (work C03).

title: When the paint happens
ask: Where should the body work and paint fall against the electrical rebuild, the luxury work and the engine swap?
why: Paint is best done after anything that drills, cuts or welds the body, but rust keeps spreading while it waits. The reshaping you asked for (D-425: bumpers, tail-light openings, spoiler, maybe a scoop and a wide body) is all cutting and welding, and the wide body waits on the wheel and suspension choice, so it has to be finished before the paint. Tint can go on at any time and is not part of this question.
options:
(a) Last: after the electrical rebuild, the luxury work and the engine swap. Nothing drilled, cut or bolted after the paint, and no chance of damaging a fresh finish while working on the car. The longest wait.
(b) Rust and body repair now, paint last. Rust stops getting worse now, the car stays drivable in primer, and the finish still goes on after everything else.
(c) Everything now, before the other projects. The car looks done soonest, but later work (the dash, doors, engine bay, harness through the firewall) risks scratches and overspray-free repairs are hard to make.
recommend: (b), unless the survey (work B02) finds almost no rust - then (a).
stops: When the body and paint work rows can start; nothing in the other projects waits on it.

title: Spoiler style
ask: What kind of spoiler do you want?
why: You ruled there is one (D-425). The FB's hatch is almost all glass, so where a spoiler can attach is limited, and each style is moulded differently.
options:
(a) A ducktail moulded into the rear panel below the hatch glass: body metal or fibreglass blended in, fixed, the most "factory" look.
(b) A lip spoiler on the hatch glass's lower edge, where Mazda fitted a rubber one on some later FBs (confirm): it opens with the hatch; bonded to the glass, painted.
(c) A wing on stands above the hatch: the most aggressive; bolted through the hatch frame, so it must look intentional to meet the seamless bar.
recommend: (a), because it is the one that reads as designed from day one, unless you want the spoiler to move with the hatch - then (b).
stops: The spoiler's design and parts, and the rear-end paint work.

title: New tail-light shape
ask: What shape should the new tail-light openings be?
why: You ruled the aperture changes (D-425). The tail-light lamp is designed in 03-luxury to fit whatever opening this project makes, so the shape here decides the lamp there. Every option must keep the legal lit area.
options:
(a) Slimmer lamps: the same width, a shorter opening, the rear panel filled and reshaped around them. Each side keeps at least 50 cm² of red for stop and turn (FMVSS 108).
(b) A full-width light bar: one continuous lamp across the rear panel, the openings joined. A modern look; the most panel work.
(c) The stock outline kept, but the lamp sunk flush into the body (frenched) with no bezel seam showing.
(d) Something else - describe it or send a picture.
recommend: (a), unless you want the rear to read as one piece - then (b).
stops: The aperture design (C08), and the luxury project's tail-light choice (03-luxury X-009).

title: Front scoop
ask: Do you want a front scoop, and if so, where and does it have to work?
why: You said maybe (D-425). A working scoop ties this project to the engine swap's hood clearance; a cosmetic one does not.
options:
(a) No scoop.
(b) A cosmetic hood scoop, moulded into the hood, closed.
(c) A working hood scoop or hood vent: it feeds the new engine's intake or lets hot air out; its shape depends on the LS's hood clearance (02-engine DS01).
(d) A front-bumper intake instead of the hood: larger openings in the new front end, feeding the radiator and brakes.
recommend: (a) no scoop, unless the LS needs the hood clearance anyway (02-engine DS01) - then (c) as a working hood vent shaped to it. Answer with what you want the car to look like; DS01 decides only whether the vent has a job.

title: Where wheels and suspension are chosen
ask: Which project should choose the wheels and the suspension that the wide body depends on?
why: You said the wide body depends on wheel choice and suspension (D-425). No project owns either today: the suspension overhaul and the steering box are planned with no project (00-CAR P-003, P-004), and the engine project owns the rear axle. Until one does, the wide body cannot be sized.
options:
(a) Add wheels and suspension to this project (04-beauty): stance is part of how the car looks, and the wide body is sized from them. The suspension overhaul (00-CAR planned P-003) comes with it.
(b) A new chassis project for wheels, tyres, suspension and the steering box (P-003, P-004); the wide body waits on its wheel choice.
(c) Put them in the engine project, which already owns the rear axle and its brakes.
recommend: (b), because suspension and steering are mechanical work unlike paint, unless you would rather keep everything about the car's look in one place - then (a).
stops: Whether there is a wide body, and its sizing (C10).

title: Tint shade
ask: How dark do you want the window tint?
why: The glass is already lightly tinted from the factory (SP-004), so any film goes on top of that and the finished window is darker than the film's number says. Colorado law (C.R.S. 42-4-227, S-153, read 2026-09-26): the windshield must pass at least 70% of light; every other window at least 27%, measured on the finished glass; a strip across the top 4 in of the windshield is allowed if it is not red or amber and does not reflect; metallic or mirrored film is prohibited on every window, with no percentage that makes it legal; the windows behind the driver may go darker than 27% only if the windshield and the front side windows both pass 70% - so a darker rear needs a meter reading of the factory front glass first. The shade decides which film is bought (work C04) and whether the car passes a roadside check.
options:
(a) Film on the side windows and the hatch glass so the finished glass passes 27% light - the installer meters it - plus a non-reflective strip on the top 4 in of the windshield. Noticeably dark, a cooler cabin, legal on every window; a ceramic film gives the heat rejection without the mirror look the law bans.
(b) Lighter, about 35-50% finished: less privacy, easier to see out at night, still cooler in a ceramic film. Legal.
(c) Darker than 27% on the rear side windows and the hatch only, legal only if the windshield and the front side windows meter at 70% or more with the factory tint - otherwise it is a ticket and an inspection problem; say so if you want it anyway and C04 adds the meter reading first.
(d) No film at all: the factory glass is already lightly tinted (the GS came that way).
recommend: (a), in a ceramic film for the heat rejection, unless night visibility matters more to you - then (b).
stops: The tint film parts round (work C04).

title: What replaces the bumpers
ask: With the big black bumpers gone, what should the front and rear ends be?
why: You ruled the bumpers go (D-425). Something still has to carry the licence plate, the plate lamp, the front turn/side lamps and possibly the hidden radar detector's sensors (03-luxury block 03.12), and every choice must look factory-built. What the law needs (C06, S-154, S-155): the rear plate horizontal with its bottom edge at least 12 in off the ground and within 18 in of the rear bumper, its lamp lit with the head lamps; tail lamps between 20 and 72 in, reflectors between 20 and 60 in; no Colorado statute found that requires a passenger car to have bumpers at all. What is sold for this car (C06, S-156, S-157, prices 2026-09-26): one true front bumper replacement, the Carbon Creations GP-1 in fiberglass, USD 308, in primer, which needs test-fitting, trimming, filling and paint and custom brackets; and Kaminari's add-on FRP pieces for the 1981-85 body - air dam spoiler 384, rear valance skirt 384, side skirts 514, a 4-piece lip kit 1,034 - which sit on the factory panels and must be blended in to meet the seamless bar. No rear bumper replacement was found for sale; the rear end is custom whatever you choose.
options:
(a) Slim body-colour bumper covers moulded to the body front and rear: a urethane or fibreglass cover shaped to flow into the fenders and quarters, with a hidden steel or aluminium bar behind each for the lamps, the plate and a minor knock. The cleanest "designed that way" look; custom shaping work front and rear (confirm cost with a shop, C03).
(b) The Carbon Creations GP-1 front bumper (USD 308 in primer) blended in, and a custom rear to match it: the front shape exists, the rear is made to it. Less shaping than (a) at the front; the rear is the same work as (a).
(c) No bumpers at all: the front and rear panels finished smooth with a small lip. The most minimal look; nothing takes a parking knock, and the plate, its lamp and the front lamps need new homes that still meet the heights above.
recommend: (a), unless the GP-1's shape is what you want at the front - then (b), which saves the front shaping and keeps the rear custom either way.
stops: The bumper design, the front and rear lamp positions, and where the hidden detector's sensors can go.

title: Which black parts go
ask: Beyond the bumpers, which of the black exterior parts should become body colour or disappear?
why: You ruled the chunky black trim goes (D-425). Which black parts count as chunky is your eye, and it decides how many holes are filled and how much is painted. From the factory parts catalogue (C07, S-005), the black exterior parts on a 1982 GS are: the front and rear bumpers with their slides and protectors (going, block on what replaces them); the rear finisher - the black panel between the tail lights; the cowl grille under the windshield and its protector; the two extractor grilles on the hatch pillars; the radiator grille; the front air dam; the rear spoiler; the drip mouldings along the roof; the outer door handles; the front and rear ornaments; the antenna. Not in the catalogue under those names and to be confirmed against your survey photos (B02): the door mirrors, the body-side protector mouldings and the window-surround rubbers.
options:
(a) Everything body colour: the side mouldings deleted and their clip holes filled, the rear finisher between the tail lights, the mirrors and the door handles painted body colour; the grilles (cowl, extractor, radiator) either body colour or replaced by openings finished smooth. One-colour, the cleanest look, the most filling and painting.
(b) Body colour except the glass trim: the rubber and black trim around the windows and windshield and the drip mouldings stay black (they frame the glass the way modern cars do); everything else goes body colour. Less work on the parts that are hardest to paint well.
(c) A deliberate accent: delete the chunky mouldings and the rear finisher's black, and keep a few chosen parts in gloss black - for example the mirrors, the grilles and the rear spoiler - say which in words.
recommend: (b), unless you want the car to read as a single colour - then (a).
stops: The list of trim to remove and holes to fill (C02), and the paint's extent (C03).
